methodology: Harness-related repositories absent by exact owner/name from tracked fak docs were ranked by direct seam relevance, current development activity, adoption signal, and license clarity. Stars are a discovery signal, not a quality claim; checked revisions and push timestamps make each observation reproducible.

repositories.why: Direct meta-harness overlap: multi-agent swarms, Codex and Claude integration, memory, skills, MCP, hooks, and a declared harness surface; 47 commits in the seven-day discovery window make it the hottest close seam.
Closest fleet-control analogue: plans work, spawns coding agents, isolates them in worktrees, and handles CI, reviews, and merge conflicts; at least 100 commits in the seven-day discovery window.
Active asynchronous coding-agent harness with sandbox, task lifecycle, desktop, evaluation, and session surfaces; 80 commits in the seven-day discovery window expose useful operating-loop seams.
Cross-harness plugin for Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, and peers with plan-review-work-compound loops and portable agent assets; 20 commits in the seven-day discovery window.
Largest adoption signal among previously untracked harness-adjacent sources and a portable skills, hooks, planning, testing, and subagent-development methodology spanning Codex and other agents.

Local TensorBuild snapshot deeply studied for transferable identity, evidence-tier, artifact-reachability, operator-surface, disambiguation, and work-cost mechanisms; surviving gaps filed as #6874-#6876. Revision history and license remain unavailable, so concepts only were borrowed.

Unified agent resource substrate deeply studied for snapshot drift gates, typed per-operation backend capabilities, transactional workspace branches, policy placement, and observer fidelity. The surviving fak gap is a strict pre-effect external-input drift contract; stronger or already-planned fak work covers the other candidates.

Transparent full-computer agent deeply studied for lifecycle hooks, plugin composition, hierarchical delegation, semantic memory, effect snapshots, connectors, and scheduling. FAK already covers the central kernel mechanisms with stronger policy, isolation, and witness boundaries; browser/office/vector-memory breadth remains modular.

Kubernetes-native distributed-inference assembly deeply studied for pluginized endpoint routing, exact KV-event locality, flow control, P/D topology, workload-variant autoscaling, and executable guide contracts. FAK should interoperate rather than duplicate its control plane; the surviving gaps are an ownership-explicit v0.9 integration refresh and a live compatibility witness.

Plugin-first agent harness deeply studied for reversible effect ownership, transactional composition replacement, durable model-visible events, standing session generations, guarded filesystem identity/version semantics, and real-composition tests. One net-new FAK gap survived as #8222; the other strongest candidates map to existing work or deliberate static-binary/default-deny divergences.

Broad artifact-scored professional-work benchmark deeply studied for official hidden-reference grading, run-local ALE-Claw gateway composition, typed trajectories, timeout-aware artifact scoring, and cross-harness controls. One FAK benchmark-entry spine survived as #8223; ALE trajectory evidence was folded into #6629.

Training-free trajectory selector deeply studied at its Terminal-Bench 2.1 self-verification seam. The candidate-pool Pass@1/oracle columns reproduce, but verifier means/error bars lack committed score/result/uncertainty artifacts and current source has cache/tournament correctness gaps. FAK already owns live best-of-N and evidence hierarchy; one provenance-bound offline selector replay survived as #8230.

The There Is No Address essay and its editorial history were studied as a cross-vendor disaggregation warning: public transport addresses stop before consumer-private locality. FAK can mitigate the split with a consumer-owned route-by-reference, terminal receipts, and full-route pricing; surviving leaves are #8259 and #8261.

NIXL was deeply studied at its descriptor, registration, remote-metadata, backend-selection, lifecycle, telemetry, and release seams. It is the transfer adapter beneath the essay, not an address-free universal memory model; FAK should govern consumer-ready route admission and receipts above it.
